items.titel: Ag/Ti Electrodes for Electrochemical Nitrate Reduction: Revealing Highly Effective Interfaces by In‐Situ Electrochemical Mass Spectrometry
items.samenvatting_bron: The electrochemical reduction of nitrate to hydroxyl amine or ammonia is a prominent means to effectively valorize agricultural effluent emissions. We demonstrate that bimetallic electrodes, composed of Ag nanoparticles deposited on Ti metal, exhibit a pronounced synergy in nitrate reduction in acidic electrolyte. This is evidenced by in‐situ electrochemical mass spectrometry (EC‐MS), showing NO evolution in a complex potential‐dependent profile at lower onset potentials compared to single metal Ag or Ti electrodes. Furthermore, liquid phase analysis shows a significant Faradaic efficiency to hydroxylamine for Ag/Ti electrodes, even at potentials above 0 V RHE , i.e., requiring at least a 200–300 mV lower overpotential than necessary for the single metal electrodes. We discuss favorable NO and hydroxylamine formation to be occurring on highly effective Ag/Ti interfaces. This work highlights the importance of interfaces and suggests that optimization of (Ag/Ti) bimetallic electrodes appears to be a valuable means to develop high performance electrodes for the reduction of nitrate in acidic conditions.

items.titel: Multiscenario Simulation and Prediction of Urban Green Space in the Changle District of Fuzhou City, China, Based on Multiobjective Optimization and a GeoSOS-FLUS Model
items.samenvatting_bron: Abstract Green spaces in densely urbanized areas along China’s southeast coast generally face spatial competition between ecological protection and development intensity, as well as conflicts between policy-oriented and market-driven values. Among them, Changle District in Fuzhou City, as the core area of the coastal new city, needs to coordinate its green space system to address complex three-dimensional problems. To explore the optimal configuration of green spaces under different ecological constraints and achieve a balance between ecological, economic, and social benefits, this paper takes Changle District in Fuzhou City as the research area, with 2020 as the base year, and innovatively combines a multiobjective optimization model with the Geographic Simulation and Optimization System–Future Land Use Simulation (GeoSOS-FLUS) model. The former is used to balance multiple objectives such as ecological conservation, economic development, and social needs, generating optimal allocation schemes. The latter precisely simulates the dynamic evolution of green spaces based on these schemes. Together, they overcome the limitations of traditional models, which cannot account for economic and ecological benefits when simulating complex urban land use. Based on this model combination, this paper simulates and predicts the area structure, spatial configuration, and target benefits of green space in Changle District in 2030 under ecological high-, medium-, and low-constraint scenarios.

items.titel: A multi-source approach for the detection and diversity assessment of avian schistosomes (Trematoda, Schistosomatidae) in freshwater ecosystems
items.samenvatting_bron: Avian schistosomes (AS) are trematodes of significant medical importance as the causative agents of cercarial dermatitis, a re-emerging waterborne human disease. Their monitoring has traditionally relied on examination of snail hosts; however, this approach is time-consuming, requires taxonomic expertise and often underestimates their diversity due to low prevalence of infection. Although environmental DNA (eDNA)-based methods have shown promise in detecting AS, most studies have employed species-specific assays that restrict the discovery of novel genetic lineages. This study integrated three complementary methodologies to comprehensively assess AS diversity in Central Europe: (i) metabarcoding of environmental water samples from various localities; (ii) metabarcoding of naturally infected snail hosts to detect pre-patent stages and (iii) standard parasitological examination and collection of cercariae released from snail hosts. In total, 34 species/genetic lineages were detected at 19 localities. Of these, three species were identified by all three techniques, two lineages by both water sample and snail tissue metabarcoding; 17 exclusively through water sample metabarcoding, 10 only in snail tissues and two solely by the standard method. items.titel: As open as possible, as protected as necessary: Proportionate governance for environmental DNA under the BBNJ Agreement
items.samenvatting_bron: The Agreement on the Conservation and Sustainable Use of Marine Biological Diversity of Areas Beyond National Jurisdiction (BBNJ Agreement) establishes new arrangements for activities involving marine genetic resources and the sharing of resulting benefits. Direct pathways to resource utilisation are most apparent in conventional genetic workflows where whole organisms or tissues are collected for biodiscovery and analysed to generate high-resolution genomic or biochemical information. By comparison, routine environmental DNA (eDNA) research generally uses non-invasive sampling to infer species presence and characterise biological communities from mixed genetic material. Evolving genomic technologies are expanding the information recoverable from both tissue-based and environmental samples, making sample source alone an insufficient indicator of intended use, information sensitivity, or potential for resource utilisation. This perspective identifies proportionate, use-based governance as an approach to fulfilling applicable BBNJ obligations while recognising routine eDNA observation as shared environmental knowledge infrastructure and supporting timely data exchange and responsive biodiversity monitoring. Ecological assessments were combined with sediment clogging measurements using the Kolmameter, with outflow reduction serving as a proxy for colmation. items.titel: Tracking the evolution of urban resilience: A systematic review of research themes and trends over two decades
items.samenvatting_bron: Urban resilience has become central to global urban policymaking as cities confront growing challenges from climate change, disasters, and socio-economic disruptions. However, research in this field spans multiple disciplines and perspectives, leaving insights fragmented across a vast body of literature. Here we provide the most comprehensive synthesis to date, analyzing over 1400 documents during 2000–2023 to trace its evolution, identify key themes, and highlight future research directions. We show that urban resilience research spans 96 countries, but over 60% comes from China, the USA, the UK, and the Netherlands. Priorities also vary due to differing development contexts. Developed countries emphasize ecological solutions and public services, backed by strong institutions and long-term climate adaptation strategies, while developing countries focus on infrastructure and technology to tackle immediate urbanization challenges. Urban resilience themes generally sit in four main frameworks: ecosystems and sustainable cities; climate change and urban governance; disaster vulnerability and community resilience; and regional and economic resilience. items.titel: A scale-invariant framework for integrating nature-based solutions into dense urban areas to improve accessibility and equity of access to urban blue and green spaces
items.samenvatting_bron: Improving accessibility and spatial equity of access to Urban Blue and Green Spaces (UB&GS) could potentially benefit biodiversity and urban sustainability. Nature-Based Solutions (NBS), serving as small-scale decentralised forms of UB&GS, can enhance both environmental quality and human well-being by fostering positive interactions between humans and the natural environment. While there is growing interest in assessing the spatial distribution of UB&GS at multiple scales, existing evaluations commonly examine each spatial scale separately. Consequently, the intrinsic scaling relationships of UB&GS and the potential of NBS integration to improve accessibility and spatial equity of access across scales remain insufficiently explored. To address this gap, this study develops a scale-invariant framework based on Universal Multifractal (UM) theory to support the integration of NBS into existing UB&GS across various spatial scales, using Paris as a case study. Then, the fractal dimension ( D F ) and Gini index are employed as indicators to assess the effectiveness of NBS in enhancing accessibility and spatial equity of access to UB&GS, respectively. The results demonstrate that the developed scale-invariant framework can effectively support the optimal integration of NBS into the current UB&GS. items.titel: Mapping Digital Platforms and Their Infrastructural Foundations for Biodiversity: A Bibliometric Analysis
items.samenvatting_bron: ABSTRACT Biodiversity loss is increasingly recognized as a grand challenge requiring new forms of innovation, coordination, and knowledge integration across organizational and institutional boundaries. While digital technologies have substantially advanced how biodiversity is monitored, measured, and managed, less is known about how digital platforms and their underlying infrastructures can support innovation processes aimed at biodiversity protection and regeneration. This paper offers a comprehensive bibliometric analysis of research connecting digital platforms, their infrastructural foundations, and biodiversity, based on a dataset of 528 scientific publications. Using co‐citation and keyword co‐occurrence analyses, the study maps the intellectual structure and evolution of this emerging field and identifies five promising research frontiers: platform governance for collective action, biodiversity data infrastructures, innovation for biodiversity, digital platforms as innovation intermediaries, and the orchestration of scalable nature‐based solutions. Building on these findings, the paper develops an integrative framework explaining how platform design and governance shape organizational coordination, knowledge integration, and innovation mechanisms, ultimately influencing biodiversity outcomes.
